notes:
Lead source: inbound marketing form (webinar on prompt efficiency). Early-stage SMB, B2C ecommerce tools; team building a conversational order-tracking + returns assistant. Key context:
- Wants a self-serve hosted option (fast onboarding) — lean infra team (2 infra ppl).
- Primary ask: reduce per-user API cost. Specifically asked about batching, KV/prefix caching, and how Redwood's Optimize recommendations could be applied to their workload.
- Quoted from call: "We need to cut token spend in half or this won't be sustainable at scale."
- Workload: mix of short chat sessions (~5-12 turns) and doc-search reranks for receipts/manuals. Est. 10k requests/day during promo peaks, average prompt size ~350 tokens, responses ~150 tokens.
- Latency tolerance: 200–400ms p50, p95 < 800ms acceptable for web chat. Throughput: bursts up to 60 qps during campaigns.
- Model preference: open to Llama2-variants or smaller curated models; cost-sensitivity prefers quantized variants if quality preserved. Wants fallback policy if cheaper model causes hallucinations.
- Data residency: US only preferred but flexible. Minimal retention needs; legal asked about retention controls and ability to purge transcripts.
- Security: require SSO/SAML for admin console and audit logs, SOC2 soon-to-be-requested by procurement. KMS not required for POC.
- POC ask: 2-week hosted POC to demonstrate ~30–50% token cost reduction via batching + prefix caching + prompt compression and to produce a token usage audit report. Also wants a sample rollout plan to production with estimated monthly cost at 100k monthly requests.
- Proposed POC steps discussed: 1) ingest sample prompts, run baseline token audit, 2) apply prompt compression templates + canonical prompts, 3) enable prefix/KV caching on dialogue turns, 4) enable mild batching at the edge, 5) measure latency and cost, iterate.
- Tech notes: using serverless edge functions; concerned batching will add latency—wants guidance on smart-routing vs aggressive batching.
- Pricing sensitivity: if presented with transparent per-token math and sample savings, more likely to convert self-serve -> paid.
- Sales hint: small logo, high churn risk but fast trial-to-paid if cost savings materialize.
- Next immediate items for Redwood: run token audit (Priya to get access to sample logs), provide an Optimize checklist + rough cost model, propose POC credit amount.
- Documents shared: security FAQ, hosted pricing deck (links in drive).
